_comment: Which SKILL a question should reach for. One case per line: the question a rep would type, and the tool we expect the model to call first. `alsoOk` lists tools that are defensible rather than wrong — a near-miss that still answers the question is not a failure, and marking it one would train us to write worse descriptions. `avoid` is the opposite: a tool that would answer plausibly and wrongly, which is the failure worth catching.

cases.q: How much revenue will we close in October 2026?
cases.why: A future period. won_value_by_month is HISTORY — answering with it would report what was won, not what is expected.

cases.q: What is the total value of our open deals right now?
Is our forecast growing month on month?
cases.why: forecast_by_month has the months but no change columns — the model would have to subtract across rows, which is where it makes arithmetic errors.

cases.q: Break the forecast down by rep — who has the most pipeline?
How many opportunities are open versus won versus lost?
Which deals make up the October forecast?
cases.why: They asked WHICH deals, not how much — a total answers a different question.

cases.q: What are the biggest deals in our pipeline?
Why can't we trust the forecast?
How many open deals have no expected close date?
Which deals keep slipping?
cases.why: Stagnant is 'nobody has spoken to it'. Slipping is 'the close date keeps moving'. A deal can be either without the other.

cases.q: How much value is at risk from slipping deals?
How much did we win last month?
cases.why: The mirror of forecast-month: this is history, and answering with the forecast view would report expectation as fact.

cases.q: Are enquiries up or down this year?
Which stage do we lose the most deals at?
Which rep closes best once a quote is out?
Who is slowest to reply to customers?
Which open deals have nothing booked on them?
Why are we losing deals?
Which lead source brings in the most revenue?
Which postcode areas do we win most in?
Has our no-task rate improved since last month?
cases.why: The no-task view is a snapshot of TODAY. Only pipeline_trend has history, so answering from the snapshot would present one day as a trend.

cases.q: Tell me about the Riverside Barn deal
cases.why: A named deal is a lookup, not an analytics question. A skill would return a filtered list and miss the messages and history.
